full_judgment:
12. Admittedly there was a Niskor Taluk in the name of Mohesh Chandra Narayan Chowdhury within Bhulua Zamindary. There is no gainsaying the fact that the suit land is part of Niskor Taluk appertaining to Mouza Ander Manik. The plaintiffs' case is that the suit land appertains to estate plot Nos. 17, 21, 26 and 27 in the Estate Map prepared by Elahi Baksha Amin of Baksha Ali Estate. The defendants claimed that these estate plots attract the diara plot or the suit plots. In paragraph 8 of the written statement, the defendants stated to have purchased 6.64 acres of land of estate plot Nos. 9, 15, 21, 27, 10, 16, 22 and 28 of the Estate Map of the then Talukders. The deeds of sale, Exhibits A and A(1) of defendant No. 1 contain the above mentioned estate plots. Therefore, it appears that the estate plot Nos. 21 and 27 are common in both the lands. The plaintiffs' further case is that Mohesh Chandra Narayan Chowdhury gave an ejara of land of Ander Manik Mouza of the Niskor Taluk to one Ainuddin Patwary for 17 years for collection of rents from the tenants by patta kabuliyat dated 29th Poush 1292 BS marked as Exhibit-3, but before the expiry of this ejara period Mohesh Chandra Narayan Chowdhury created a Sarbapori Kayami Mokarary Taluk in respect of the land of this ejara patta, Exhibit 3, in the name of Baksha Ali Patwary by a patta dated 25th Agrahayan 1298 BS, marked Exhibit-2. The plaintiffs stated the origin of his suit land from Ejara patta dated 29th Poush 1292 BS (Exhibit-3). The plaintiff as PW 2 stated in his deposition that a Taluk, namely, Ainuddin Miajee was mentioned in Exhibit 3. Ainuddin Miajee as stated in the written statement of defendant No. 1 and Ainuddin Miajee as stated in Exhibit-3 is the same person. Exhibit-3 contains several Taluks and there is a mention of Taluk, Ainuddin Miajee and Omaruddin Hajee and from the above fact, it appears that the land contained in the deed of sale of defendant No. 1 got its origin in Exhibit-3. The plaintiff as PW2 in his cross-examination stated that Ainuddin had a son Ali Mia and that Ali Mia had two sons named Fazlul Haque and Sultan Ahmed. Defendant No. 1 stated to have purchased the suit land from Fazlul Haque and Sultan Ahmed by two registered deeds of sale dated 3-12-1957. 

 13. The trial Court came to a finding that the plaintiffs and the contesting defendant drew the origin of the disputed land from the ejara patta (Exhibit-3) and that it could not be said that the deeds of defendant No. 1 were absolutely bogus. The trial Court also found that the deeds of sale of defendant No. 1 were coupled with possession and that defendant No. 1 had been possessing the suit land from the time of his purchase.
